parts.text: In this experiment, you will determine the focal length of a converging lens by two methods. Refer to Fig. 3.1. Fig. 3.1

parts.label: a
parts.text: (a) Set up the apparatus as shown in Fig. 3.1. Set the distance u between the illuminated object and the lens to 20.0 cm. Switch on the lamp. Place the screen near the lens. Move the screen until a sharp image of the illuminated object is seen on the screen.

ms.label: 3(a)(i)
ms.text: move screen slowly / back and forth

parts.label: ii
parts.text: (ii) Measure v , the distance from the lens to the screen as indicated in Fig. 3.1. v = ..........................................................cm Measure h O , the height of the illuminated object, indicated in Fig. 3.1. h O = ..........................................................cm Measure h I , the height of the image on the screen. h I = ..........................................................cm [2] Switch off the lamp.

ms.label: 3(a)(ii)
ms.text:
v between 40.0 (cm) and 100.0 (cm)
ho between 1.5 (cm) and 2.5 (cm) and hi > ho

parts.label: iii
parts.text: (iii) Calculate a value M for the magnification, using the equation M = h I h O . M = ......................................................... [1]

ms.label: 3(a)(iii)
ms.text: correct calculation of M and no unit

parts.label: b
parts.text: (b) Calculate a value f 1 for the focal length of the lens. Use your values from (a)(ii) and (a)(iii) and the equation f 1 = v ( M + 1) . Give an appropriate unit. f 1 = ......................................................... [2]

ms.label: 3(b)
ms.text:
f1 in range 12.0 to 18.0
unit of cm – seen at least once and not contradicted

ms.label: 3(c)
ms.text:
any one valid difficulty (e.g. hand or ruler gets in way of light)
one improvement to overcome the difficulty (e.g. translucent screen (and measure from back) / fix grid to screen)

parts.label: d
parts.text: (d) Adjust the position of the lens so that u = 40.0 cm. Switch on the lamp. Place the screen near the lens. Move the screen until a sharp image of the illuminated object is seen on the screen. Measure the distance v between the lens and the screen as indicated in Fig. 3.1. v = .................................................... cm [1] Switch off the lamp.

parts.label: e
parts.text: (e) Calculate a second value f 2 for the focal length of the lens. Use your values from (d) and the equation f 2 = uv ( u + v ) . f 2 = ......................................................... [1]

ms.label: 3(f)
ms.text:
f2 with reason
e.g.: f2 as f1 has smaller measurements (i.e. ho and hi) (and so % uncertainties larger)
